work.title: Reversible Parallel Evidence-First Workbench Frontend
authority: Direct user instruction to implement a reversible parallel clean-room frontend at apps/workbench/public/next/index.html.
Project Redwood non-negotiable invariant: unreconciled differences must be surfaced and never silently forced to balance.

intent.productGoal: Give professional reviewers a calm, evidence-first parallel Workbench presentation without altering canonical economics, evidence, gates, workbook behavior, or the existing root UI.
intent.capability: Serve an isolated /next frontend that reads and writes only existing Workbench canonical API/run state and presents all seven canonical phases—Intake, Map, Reconcile, Migration evidence, Analyze, Review, and Export—with evidence, uncertainty, and decision lenses; Intake carries current and prior-comparison scope dates to the existing canonical API.
architecturalIntent: The /next path is a static parallel surface under public/next and does not replace or import the root frontend.
Canonical API endpoints and persisted run state remain the only operational authority; the frontend performs no financial calculation.
Observed evidence, derived results, reviewer candidates, decisions, and release authority remain explicitly separated.
invariants: The root path and all existing backend, calculations, fixtures, gates, source evidence, and workbook behavior remain unchanged.
Unreconciled differences, blocked gates, quarantine, and uncertainty remain visible rather than normalized or concealed.
Reviewer actions use existing run-bound API endpoints and do not imply professional approval or client release.
acceptanceEvidence: Static build copies /next assets into apps/workbench/dist/next without changing root artifacts.
JavaScript syntax validation covers the new frontend asset.
A controlled local server observation confirms /, /next/index.html, and canonical run endpoints are reachable and that the root asset checksum remains unchanged after the parallel implementation.

decisions.decision: Implement the new experience as standalone static HTML, CSS, and JavaScript under public/next.
decisions.rationale: This makes the UI reversible by removing the directory and keeps the existing root experience untouched.

decisions.decision: Use only established API endpoints and fields already consumed by the current public Workbench, plus the existing run lookup needed to load a persisted canonical run by URL.
decisions.rationale: This preserves canonical calculation and governance authority while avoiding backend or workbook scope changes.

decisions.decision: Treat missing monetary values as unavailable, require an active canonical release record in addition to G7, and reload the run after review writes.
decisions.rationale: The presentation must not turn absent evidence into zero, infer release authority from G7 alone, or display stale gate state.

observedBehaviour: The server served the legacy root (200), the isolated /next/index.html entry (200), and the /next JavaScript asset (200) concurrently.

Persisted canonical run c8f21c7f-82a5-47a1-9d21-ab78af14660a returned four reconciliations, one finding, eight gates, seven source-inventory entries, and blocked G7; the parallel UI consumes those fields directly.

Persisted migration run 3f1715a9-4c60-4097-bb11-d141f29b3d04 exposed canonical migration evidence with four source-system contributions, two crosswalk-coverage records, and passed G4; the new Migration evidence phase renders this state without calculation or normalization.
The parallel Intake form exposes prior-comparison start and end dates and sends both values as priorComparableStart and priorComparableEnd within the existing canonical scope payload.

The root index and root app JavaScript had no working-tree diff and retained SHA-256 values B093104A6DFA5776CE5ECB5B972731369EB0F0B9BF132B6E37C899AA5E80313E and 383D64F2C9C45E0B419D98FFB16FF20A115A4BD6FA0D404551CA52FA3E6DFC8A.

evidence.reference: apps/workbench: node --check public/next/workbench-next.js; pnpm run build
evidence.result: Syntax check passed and the static build copied public/next into dist/next.

evidence.reference: Controlled server on PORT=4174: GET /, GET /next/index.html, GET /next/workbench-next.js, GET /api/runs/c8f21c7f-82a5-47a1-9d21-ab78af14660a, GET /api/runs/3f1715a9-4c60-4097-bb11-d141f29b3d04
evidence.result: All requested resources returned 200; the canonical run exposed the expected evidence and gate state.

evidence.reference: git diff -- apps/workbench/public/index.html apps/workbench/public/app.js apps/workbench/server.mjs apps/workbench/build.mjs
evidence.result: No diff; the root UI and backend/static-serving implementation were not changed.

divergences.expected: The existing static server would resolve /next/ to the parallel entry document.
divergences.observed: The unchanged static-file server has no directory-index rewrite, so the supported parallel entry is /next/index.html.

learning.recurringPattern: Parallel static frontends can preserve authority boundaries when they consume raw canonical run state rather than duplicating calculation logic.
learning.improvementProposal: If /next becomes a retained product route, add a separately approved directory-index rule or an explicit route registry without changing this clean-room surface's API contract.
durableKnowledge: The current Workbench static server serves nested public assets directly but does not rewrite a directory request to index.html.
The parallel frontend must be opened at /next/index.html and may load a persisted run with ?run=<canonical-run-id>.
